purpose: Perampanel is used to help control seizures in people with epilepsy. It can be used for partial-onset seizures (seizures that start in one part of the brain) and also for a type called primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures. It is usually used along with other seizure medications.
how_it_works: In epilepsy, certain brain cells become overexcited and fire off signals that cause seizures. Perampanel works by blocking a specific receptor in the brain called the AMPA receptor, which is like turning down the volume on that overexcitement. By calming these overactive signals, it helps reduce the number and severity of seizures.
common_side_effects: Dizziness and feeling unsteady or off-balance are the most common side effects. You may also feel sleepy, tired, or have headaches. Some people notice irritability, problems with memory or concentration, or blurred vision. These effects are often worse when you first start the medication or when your dose goes up.
warnings: This medication carries a serious warning about changes in mood or behavior — some people feel more angry, aggressive, irritable, or have thoughts of hurting themselves or others. Tell your doctor or pharmacist right away if you or a loved one notices unusual mood or behavior changes. Because it causes dizziness and sleepiness, do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medication, as it can make dizziness and aggression much worse. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can trigger more seizures.
typical_dosing: Perampanel is taken by mouth once a day, usually at bedtime to help reduce dizziness. Adults typically start at a low dose of 2 mg per night, and the doctor slowly increases it every week or two based on how well it is working and how you tolerate it. The usual effective dose is between 4 mg and 12 mg per night. Your doctor will find the right dose for you.
